feedback: Based only on iteration 0 (the symmetric baseline: sensors at y=0.04 m, x=-0.02..+0.02 m, kp 2.0, ki 0, kd 0.05, base_speed 1.6). Every one of its 60 trials ended off_track. Progress was 0.04 on the s-bend and 0.115 on the oval, max_error was about 0.061 m (the 0.06 m floor), and rms_error was about 0.03 m. Steering oscillation was low (0.07 to 0.16), so the failure is steady outward drift on bends, not jitter. What I had to compensate for in the controller: the weights had to stay sign-correct, and a small integral term was needed to counter the fixed left/right motor mismatch. The integral was added in my package, not as a geometry change. Next race, the change depends on the result. If max_error still reaches about 0.06 m on the s-bend with the new geometry (turn authority still limiting), widen the sensor span further or raise the sensor offset to y=0.08 to see the bend earlier, keeping wheel_track at 0.10 m. If line_loss_events rise with the wider array (outer sensors losing the tape at the edges), return the outer sensors to x=±0.025 m. If steering_oscillation grows with the lighter body (too fast), increase mass to 0.7 kg or wheel_track to 0.12 m to add damping. If progress rises on the oval but completion is still missed on time, this supports the lightness and sensor-lookahead changes, so keep them.
requested_changes: If max_error stays near 0.06 m on the s-bend with the new array: test sensor y at 0.08 m (the contract maximum) to see bends earlier, keeping x at ±0.03 m, since iteration 0 showed drift outward on the sharpest bend with y=0.04 m.

If line_loss_events rise above the iteration 0 values (1 on oval and s-bend, 2 on slalom) with the wider array: reduce the outer sensor spread to x=±0.025 m, because the outer sensors are losing the 25 mm tape at the edges.

If steering_oscillation grows above the iteration 0 range (0.07 to 0.16) with the lighter body: raise mass to 0.7 kg or wheel_track to 0.12 m to add yaw damping, since the faster response needs more inertia at the same kp.
